title: Moon Dust Cutting Myths

scenes.text: Apollo 17 brought back 110 kilograms of lunar dust for study.
People think moon dust is sharp enough to slice steel like a knife.
scenes.label: Moon dust cuts steel

scenes.text: Lunar regolith is made of tiny glassy shards, but its hardness is similar to sand and it cannot cut metal.
scenes.label: Regolith can’t cut metal

scenes.text: Sharp but not lethal – the dust is abrasive, not a blade.
scenes.label: Abrasive, not cutting
scenes.sub: It can wear tools but won’t slice steel.

scenes.text: Follow for the science they never taught you.

description: The myth that moon dust can cut through steel is busted – it’s abrasive, not a cutting tool. Follow for daily science!
